Commentary.Commentary: Welcome back to the chase. The players of New Zealand have come out back in the middle, led by their skipper Michael Bracewell who gave a pep talk in a huddle before they took their positions. The two openers for Pakistan are Imam-ul-Haq and Abdullah Shafique. Will O'Rourke has the new ball in hand, and he will start the proceedings. Here we go...
... The Run Chase ...

With the first innings done, who will be the happier side? It is quite tough to say now, but New Zealand have got all the momentum with the Hay’s hitting in the last couple of overs. Now, all eyes are on their batters to chase it down. The pressure is on, especially after the criticism they faced back home for losing the T20I series and the first ODI, where they failed to chase a 300+ total. Meanwhile, New Zealand’s bowlers will feel confident as they have a good total on this surface, which has seam and swing movement, and if they can strike early in the Powerplay and remove a couple of key batters, they could put Pakistan under serious pressure. Which team will come out on top? Stay tuned, as the action of the second inning is about to begin!

Mitchell Hay is up for a quick chat. He says it was tough to start, but he had a plan with Abbas, the conversation was good, and they worked on the match up on how to reach a decent total. Shares that the score on the board is nice now and something for the bowlers to bowl. Reckons it was nice to get a couple of sixes out of the middle.

Pakistan’s bowlers justified their skipper’s decision to bowl first, delivering a disciplined performance till the 40 overs, though the 32 extra runs they conceded through wides could come back to haunt them. The introduction of leg-spinner Sufiyan Muqeem turned the game in Pakistan’s favor, as he struck in his very first over. Skipper Mohammad Rizwan rotated his bowlers smartly, ensuring no batter got too comfortable against a single bowler. The short three-to-four-over spells for each bowler worked for Pakistan, and every bowler chipped in with at least one wicket, highlighting an all-round team effort.

Despite wickets falling around him, Mitchell Hay stood tall, reaching a well-earned fifty. He built small but crucial partnerships with lower-order batters Nathan Smith, Ben Sears, and Jacob Duffy, ensuring New Zealand reached a competitive and defendable total. His inning was a perfect mix of patience and aggression at the end, displaying maturity under pressure. Interestingly, every Kiwi batter in the top 7 got into double digits, indicating they all got starts but failed to capitalize, except for Hay, who remained the standout performer with a brilliant 99 off just 78 balls.

Their struggles were short-lived as they lost their wickets in back-to-back overs, and suddenly, New Zealand went from a steady 100/2 to a shaky 102/4 in just a couple of deliveries. The rebuilding job then fell to Muhammad Abbas, the half-centurion from the previous match, and his captain Michael Bracewell. They managed to add 30 runs before Mohammad Wasim dismissed Bracewell, caught behind. The biggest partnership of the inning came next, with young Muhammad Abbas and Mitchell Hay putting together a vital 77-run stand. Their partnership helped the Kiwis recover and post a fighting total. However, just as they were looking to accelerate, Sufiyan Muqeem broke the stand, dismissing Abbas, who holed out to deep square leg after making 41 runs while trying to up the scoring rate.

New Zealand’s inning had ups and downs, but eventually, they ended at 292/8, thanks largely to Mitchell Hay’s crucial knock of 99 not-out. Though he missed out on a deserving hundred but this has been one of the best innings. The Kiwi openers started positively, finding the boundaries at regular intervals and putting up a solid 54-run stand in just 6.2 overs. Debutant Rhys Mariu looked promising but fell to a leading edge, cutting short his innings. Meanwhile, the other opener, Nick Kelly, played the aggressor in the partnership, stroking some classy boundaries on his way past the 30-runs mark. However, in his attempt to be greedy, he tried cutting a ball that wasn’t short enough and edged it straight to the keeper. With both openers gone, experienced batters Henry Nicholls and Daryl Mitchell had the responsibility to stabilize the innings, but they never looked comfortable.

Commentary.Commentary: DRINKS! A quick start despite losing two wickets from New Zealand, and they are 95/2 after the first fourteen overs. The debutant, Rhys Mariu, played a couple of good shots before pershing to a uncanny shot. He would be kicking himself for getting out in that fashion. The other opener, Nick Kelly, started on a bang as he was hitting the boundaries for fun but lost his wicket in getting too greedy. NZ have their two most experienced guy in the middle, Henry Nicholls and Daryl Mitchell, and they will bank on them to form a good partnership here to take them past 300 on this good wicket. On the other hand, Pakistan have bowled too many wide balls, but they have been able to pick two wickets. Their bowling lacks a zip, but they will have to find some motivation to take more wickets to bounce back in this game, otherwise, it will get out of their hands in a matter of time. An interesting passage of play is ahead of us, and with that, Akif Javed will continue from this end.

Commentary.Commentary: We are all set to begin! The players are making their way out to the middle now. Pakistan take up their respective field positions. Rhys Mariu and Nick Kelly are the two openers for New Zealand. Faheem Ashraf has the new ball in hand and is raring to go. Let's play...

PITCH REPORT - Franckie Mackay is pitchside with Craig McMillan. She says that the weather is a bit cloudy and the rain can interrupt the game. Craig says that the pitch has a lot of grass, so the bowlers will be pretty happy to look at that, and they will want to use that pace and bounce. Mentions that there will be a lateral movement for sure and the early overs will be crucial for both sides whether you are batting first or bowling first. States that the wicket has been rolled pretty good, and both captains will want to bowl first as the square boundaries are short, with the straight one a bit longer.

Salman Agha from Pakistan also shares a few words. He says that they lost the key moments in the first game, which they have discussed about and will look to work on in this one. Adds that they started well with the ball and Haris Rauf was brilliant but they lost their way a bit towards the end.

The debutant for New Zealand, Rhys Mariu is up for a quick chat. He says that Sam Wells called him around this breakfast and said that he is going to play today, and he was really happy to hear that news. Adds that his family is very excited about his international debut. States that all the team members welcomed him and that they have been pretty helpful to him in understanding everything. The ODI series between New Zealand and Pakistan rolls into Hamilton, where Seddon Park will host the second match of the three-game affair. The series opener was a gripping contest that swung back and forth, but in the end, the hosts prevailed to take a 1-0 lead. New Zealand will be eager to seal the series in Hamilton before heading to Mount Maunganui for the final ODI. Mark Chapman’s 132 powered the Kiwis to 344, setting the foundation for a commanding win as the bowlers stepped up to finish the job. Alongside Chapman, Daryl Mitchell and debutant Muhammad Abbas  made valuable contributions, with Abbas enjoying a memorable international debut. However, New Zealand will be without Will Young for the remainder of the series as he awaits the birth of his child. Right-handed batter Rhys Mariu has been called up and is likely to make his debut in Hamilton. On the bowling front, Nathan Smith was the standout performer, with four wickets in a disciplined collective effort. With momentum on their side, Michael Bracewell’s men are expected to stick with a winning combination. They don’t have too many options at their disposal, but should New Zealand secure the series in Hamilton, we could see Ben Sears and Adithya Ashok get a game in the third ODI. Pakistan, on the other hand, were left to rue their decision to go in with only four proper bowling options and no specialist spinner. If they are to stay alive in the series, they must shore up their bowling attack, with Abrar Ahmed and Sufiyan Muqeem available as spin options. In the batting department, they have been dealt a blow with Usman Khan ruled out of the Hamilton fixture due to a hamstring injury, with Imam-ul-Haq likely to step in. A collective effort in both departments is imperative for Pakistan as they fight to keep the series alive. Can New Zealand wrap up the series in Hamilton, or will Pakistan bounce back to set up a decider in Mount Maunganui? We shall find out.
